definition.note: Member of the C(P) family: Neovius' surface is C9(P), and the family continues by adding handles in the same 96-fold symmetric cell.  No closed form is stored: the surface is not implemented in math_art, so there is no shipped code to verify a transcription against, and an unverified formula would be worse than a null.

construction.blocked_by: Needs constraint-plane support in the area minimiser (vertices sliding on planes rather than pinned) plus the discrete adjoint/Bonnet transform. math_art/minsurf/plateau.py has neither; its `minimize_area` only pins vertices. Brakke's datafile for this surface is an ADJOINT file and cannot be used without that step.
construction.resume: K. Brakke's adjoint.cmd (mirrored in starfish.tar) is the algorithm, and U. Pinkall and K. Polthier, 'Computing discrete minimal surfaces and their conjugates', Experimental Mathematics 2(1) (1993) -- converted at research/papers/minimal-surfaces/ -- is the method. See BACKLOG.md.

provenance.definition: Not transcribed. The record exists to state that the surface is absent and why; a fabricated equation would be worse than a null.
sources: A. H. Schoen, NASA TN D-5541 (1970), for the C(P) construction.

K. A. Brakke, 'Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces', Surface Evolver example collection, kenbrakke.com/evolver/examples/periodic/periodic.html (local mirror: brakke/book/evolver/). C-P family page ch018_cpfamily.md.
